claim: The abc conjecture (Masser and Oesterlé, 1985–88) is about equations a + b = c in whole numbers with no common factor. Multiply the distinct primes dividing a, b and c to get rad(abc). Usually c is smaller than rad(abc). The conjecture says c can exceed rad(abc)^(1 + ε) only finitely often, for any ε > 0. Example: 1 + 8 = 9 has rad(1·8·9) = 6 < 9, a rare “hit”. If true, abc would imply many other results at once, including a version of Fermat’s Last Theorem for large exponents.
